title: CMC 활용 학습에서 면대면 수업 유무, 협력유형 및 메타인지가 학업성취와 상호작용에 미치는 영향

abstracts.value: 본 연구는 전통교실에 비동시적 텍스트 기반 CMC의 효과적인 활용 방안을 알아보기 위해 고등학생 86명을 대상으로 하여 면대면 수업 유무, 조별 협력학습 유형, 학습자의 메타인지가 학업성취와 상호작용에 미치는 영향을 살펴보았다. 본 연구에서 학업성취는 사실적 문제와 일반화 및 추론문제 두 가지로 분류되었고 상호작용은 CMC 메시지를 분석하여 과제관련, 사교적, 절차적 상호작용으로 분류되었다. CMC 과제가 면대면 수업과 관련이 있을 때, 자율적 협력 상황에서 학습자의 일반화 및 추론문제 점수가 높았다. 메타인지가 높은 학습자의 경우 사실적 문제와 일반화 및 추론문제 점수가 모두 높았다. 상호작용은 면대면 수업 유무, 협력학습 유형 집단간에는 의의 있는 차이가 없었지만, 메타인지 상 집단은 과제관련, 사교적, 절차적 상호작용 빈도가 모두 높았다. 본 연구결과를 통해 CMC와 면대면 의사소통의 상호보완 가능성, CMC 활용 수업 시 학습자의 메타인지가 갖는 중요성을 알 수 있다.

The purpose of this study is to identify effective methods of asynchronous text-based CMC use in traditional classrooms. For this purpose this study examined the effect of face-to-face teaching existence, the types of group collaboration(paired learning, task allotment and autonomic learning) and learner's metacognition on academic achievement and interaction. In this study academic achievement was classified into two; the first was factual questions, the second was generalization and inference questions. Interaction was classified into three after CMC messages analysis; task-related, social and procedural interaction. The subjects were 86 students from D High School in D-gun, J province. They were divided into 6 groups which were organized into two teams with 7 to 8 members and experienced learning through online conferencing using asynchronous text-based CMC.
The results of this study were as follows: First, the generalization and inference question scores were significantly higher with face-to-face teaching than without it. Therefore, it can be better to choose learning tasks related face-to-face teaching in learning through CMC. Second, the autonomic collaboration type had the highest generalization and inference question scores among three types of group collaboration. More reciprocal reference and interaction with other participants can be effective in learning through CMC. Third, there were many differences in academic achievements and interaction frequencies between upper and lower group in metacognition. For academic achievement, the upper group got better scores in both questions. For interaction, the upper group's task-related, social, procedural interaction frequency was higher. These results show metacognition is related to not only cognitive sides but also affective sides like learning motivation or interest induction. As metacognition has a strong influences on learning through CMC, especially collaborative learning situation, it is necessary to have training for improving metacognitive strategies.
